Indian chef Ranji Smile opened America’s first Indian restaurant in 1901 - then became a fake prince. One hundred and twenty-five years ago, in 1901, an Indian chef opened what was almost certainly the first Indian restaurant in the US. Ranji Smile was one of the most colourful and enigmatic figures to shape the American food scene. In the summer of 1899, Smile sailed from London to New York. We know hardly anything about his origins and early life, not even his real name. "Ranji" was probably a nod to the Indian cricketing sensation KS Ranjitsinhji, then a star attraction at Test matches in Britain. "Smile" could have been an anglicisation of "Ismail".

A century-old paper mill in Témiscaming, Quebec is indefinitely closed after the US imposed 50% tariffs on its products, putting hundreds out of work. As you cross the Ottawa river into Témiscaming, Quebec, the paper mill takes up much of the horizon. Now, the main employer and economic anchor sits idle after trade talks broke down between Canada and the US and President Donald Trump imposed more tariffs on the country.

The United States has recently struggled in alternate shot in men's pro golf team events. James delivered his best one yet — yes, in a short sample size — with the 76ers on Friday night. Bigger Than Sports, a youth-operated nonprofit organization founded by Allderdice alumni Ian and Emma Waite, is working to help high school student-athletes prepare for life after athletics. The organization gained national recognition when it received the Billie Jean King Youth Leadership Award during the 2025 ESPYs. Less than 1% of high school student-athletes go on to play professional sports, leaving many uncertain about their career paths once their playing days are over. Bigger Than Sports addresses this gap by assisting student-athletes, particularly those in marginalized areas, through weekly mentorship initiatives and fireside chats with guest speakers.

Account takeover threats go beyond stolen passwords. SIM swaps, MFA fatigue, malware and OAuth consent phishing can bypass login security even with multifactor authentication enabled. Raquel Alvarez Tabernero/Shutterstock Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover In a casual conversation, you could maybe get away with using the acronyms GPS and GNSS interchangeably. The two are closely related, in the same way that an iPhone is a type of smartphone. GNSS stands for Global Navigation Satellite System, a broad term for any satellite navigation system, including GPS. NASA describes it as providing "autonomous geospatial positioning" because, of course, they do. The most important takeaway is that GPS, as familiar as it is to everyone, is merely a type of GNSS, specifically the United States' satellite navigation system.

The Los Angeles Dodgers have six players entering arbitration this offseason, and they need to decide how to approach them. The standard number of arbitration years is three, but players in the top 22% can earn the Super Two Exception, which lets them enter arbitration a year early and get four total years. In arbitration, a team must decide whether to tender or non-tender players by November 20th. If they are tendered, they continue to arbitration; if they are non-tendered, they become free agents. Once tendered, the team and player can agree to avoid arbitration or go to a hearing, where both sides submit a salary proposal and a third-party arbitrator rules for the player or team.

DeMonica Amerson was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis at 21. Nearly two decades later, she received devastating news. DeMonica Amerson's diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in 2001 had been a shock. No one in her family had ever had the autoimmune condition, and it had been difficult to diagnose. Doctors had first thought she had optic neuritis because her symptoms were in her eyes. Then they suspected lupus. After a spinal tap, she was diagnosed with MS. At the time, Amerson had never heard about the condition. She had just graduated from college and expected to be in the prime of her life. Instead, she had to give herself daily shots to treat the condition.

From a fake fair catch to a blind field goal lateral, these college football trick plays fooled defenses and changed games Coaches spend hours watching film to find tiny mistakes in how a team lines up. A good fake handoff, a surprise pass or a player acting like he isn't part of the play can flip a game upside down in a second. Some of these crazy calls led to famous touchdowns and huge wins. Others blew up completely, but people still talk about them anyway. The best trick plays all do the same thing, they get the defense to chase a ghost. By the time the other team figures out what is going on, the ball is already gone.

CINCINNATI (AP) — Cincinnati Reds closer Emilio Pagán declined a $10 million player option for 2027 on Saturday, deciding to become a free agent.Cincinnati also declined a $16 million mutual option on third baseman/designated hitter Eugenio Suárez and an $8 million mutual option on right-hander Pierce Johnson, who gets a $1 million buyout. Pagán was 5-1 with a 3.38 ERA and 25 saves in 28 chances this year, when he had a $10 million salary . He didn't pitch for the Reds between May 5 and July 3 because of a strained left hamstring . The 35-year-old right-hander has 90 saves in 10 major league seasons, the last three with the Reds.

Cincinnati will now need to find a closer for 2027, assuming they plan on ever having a lead in the 9th inning. Emilio Pagán officially declined his option to return to the club for next season, as BBWAA writer Francys Romero reported earlier in the day. In doing so, he'll hit the market in search of another multi-year pact from someone, though in theory the Reds themselves could still be in the mix for his services on a new deal. Pagán missed nearly two months of the 2026 season after a devastating hamstring strain, though as Romero notes he returned in excellent form through the end of the season.

The British government has never formally apologised for slavery despite repeated calls from a number of Commonwealth leaders. Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he is "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but has ruled out financial reparations. He said he wanted a "dialogue with those affected" and was open to "calls for an apology", but said reparations were "not the right answer". The Hoggard girls tennis team claimed its first state title in program history with a dominant performance over Myers Park Saturday, Oct. 31. AC Milan secured a decisive 3-1 victory over rivals Inter Milan by prioritising transitional speed over possession. Starting outside linebacker Rolijah Hardy has a "shock" injury, IU coach Curt Cignetti said. Jacob Savage filled in admirably to beat Minnesota. The Golden State Valkyries won a WNBA championship by investing boldly in women’s basketball and building a winning culture from the ground up. Before Golden State ever arrived in the WNBA, it had a vision for what it wanted to be: a premier franchise with an unmatched desire for greatness. On Oct. 5, 2023, owner Joseph Lacob declared the Valkyries would win a championship within the first five years of the team's existence, a lofty goal. Still, neither Lacob nor the organization ever wavered in their pursuit. The Valkyries actually did it in two, winning the title with a 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history on Saturday, Oct. 31 at the Chase Center.

BALTIMORE (AP) — Division III Johns Hopkins used an obscure rule to win its game against Muhlenberg on Saturday, prevailing 31-28 when Kaleb Wayt made a 39-yard field goal on a fair catch kick.When a player makes a fair catch, the receiving team has the option of attempting a field goal from that spot on the next play. Every now and then, it's attempted in the NFL, sometimes from unusually long distances, and the rule was added for college before this season. With the score tied at 28, Alex Orecchio made a fair catch on a short punt at the Muhlenberg 29. Then Wayt connected on the 39-yard field goal, putting the Blue Jays ahead with two seconds remaining.

Witch hunts reached their peak in England in the 1600s. In total across England and Scotland, around 5,000 women convicted of witchcraft were executed, some by hanging and some by burning.
